roadmap_events.goal: A pptx distilling the Columbia 'MBA Transformed' symposium plus John's own AI on-ramp, substantial enough to carry ~50 minutes of discussion with Smeal's AI teaching community of practice.

steps.name: Gandalf heavy on the symposium corpus
steps.done_when: An honesty-stamped deep read of the full archive (transcripts, slides, SUMMARY.md, the Ipeirotis oral-exam folder) mapping which of the four themes each talk supports — and an explicit list of claims the corpus cannot back.
oranges_annotations: Kyle Jensen (Yale) — the agent-facing-course story you want to spotlight — has only external slides here: no video, no transcript. Decide now whether to chase the source material or scope that section to what the slides prove.
Talks 15–16 have no verified transcripts, and the NYU agents-course site you mentioned has no materials posted yet — the can't-back-this-slide list must exist before the outline hardens.
SUMMARY.md already went to this audience; a deck that re-plates it means the room has read the punchline. The deep read should mark what is NEW beyond the summary.

steps.name: researchPrime: contained-tool taxonomy
steps.done_when: A sourced survey of the chat / CLI / contained-tool landscape (CoWork-class tools, ChatGPT's equivalent, Perplexity, Gemini's offering, others named in the talks) reduced to 2–3 slide-ready categories.
oranges_annotations: This market churns monthly — organize by category, not per-product features, and date-stamp the slide, or it is stale by presentation day.
The 'do they train on your data' claim will be challenged live by faculty — each vendor's privacy stance needs a citable source, not memory.

steps.name: Design the deck and the 50 minutes
steps.done_when: A locked outline: section order, slide budget per section, one designed discussion prompt per section, and a decided demo strategy (live vs clip vs screenshot) — signed off by John.
oranges_annotations: 50 minutes of discussion is not 50 minutes of slides — without a planted question per section this becomes a lecture; the presentation/discussion split is the cheapest decision to make now and the most expensive to retrofit.
Four workshop themes plus your personal on-ramp is 60+ slides of raw material — the cutting happens here or it happens at midnight before the talk.

Playing the Ipeirotis oral-exam demo means choosing and trimming the excerpt from the local MP4 in advance — and confirming you may re-show symposium recordings to a non-symposium audience; live demos (agents, Anchor) each need a rehearsed screenshot fallback.

steps.name: Build the pptx
steps.done_when: Full deck drafted: all sections, latent-space visuals, tool-taxonomy slides, speaker notes carrying the discussion prompts.
oranges_annotations: The latent-space explanation (Dean Corey in Van Gogh / Disney style) depends on images that do not exist yet — generate and vet them before assembly, and style-rendering a real dean's likeness for a faculty room may warrant his nod first.
Smeal template and branding are cheap applied from slide one, painful retrofitted onto a finished deck.

steps.name: Fact-check, timing run, sign-off
steps.done_when: Every speaker/school/tool attribution verified against the transcripts, a timed rehearsal fits the slot, and John approves the final deck.
oranges_annotations: Every 'the guy from Yale/NYU/Columbia' must become a verified name before facing a community of practice — your 'vetting tool inside Excel at Columbia' is plausibly Guetta's XLKitLearn, but that is exactly the kind of guess this stage exists to kill.
Offering Anchor and materials from the podium creates follow-up commitments — decide what is actually shareable, in what state, before promising it.

default_prompts: What would John ask next about this stage?
What artifact must exist before the stage can close?
What decision, if any, requires a human gate?
